questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of 'bring about' in: 'The new policy brought about significant changes in education.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. BRING ABOUT = to cause something to happen. 'The policy brought about changes' = the policy caused those changes. Synonyms: cause, produce, result in, give rise to.

questions.stem: 'The meeting was called off at the last minute.' What does 'called off' mean?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CALL OFF = to cancel something that had been planned. 'The meeting was called off' = the meeting was cancelled. Distinguish: cancelled (permanent) vs postponed (moved to later). 'Called off' means cancelled entirely.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 'She had to ______ her presentation several times before it was approved.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. GO OVER = to review or check something carefully. 'Go over the presentation' = review it multiple times. Give up = quit; put down = write down or criticise; set aside = reserve for later.

questions.stem: 'He eventually came around to our way of thinking.' 'Came around' means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. COME AROUND = to change one's opinion; to be persuaded. 'Came around to our thinking' = gradually changed his mind to agree with us. Other meanings: come around = visit informally, or regain consciousness (context determines meaning).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 'The company plans to ______ its old equipment with newer models.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. PHASE OUT = to gradually discontinue or withdraw something. 'Phase out old equipment' = gradually stop using it and replace with new models. Pick up = collect/improve; break down = stop working/analyse; take off = leave/become successful.

questions.stem: 'The charity event fell through despite months of planning.' 'Fell through' means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. FALL THROUGH = to fail to happen; to not be completed. 'The event fell through' = the event did not happen, despite planning. 'Despite months of planning' reinforces the disappointment of failure.

questions.stem: 'The new employee was slow to ______ with the company's procedures and culture.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. CATCH ON = to begin to understand or become familiar with something. 'Slow to catch on with procedures' = slow to understand and adapt. Catch up = reach the same level as others; catch out = expose someone in a lie/mistake.

questions.stem: 'The opposition tried to ______ the new bill by prolonging the debate.' The correct phrasal verb is:
questions.explanation: A is correct. HOLD UP = to delay or obstruct something. 'Hold up the bill by prolonging debate' = deliberately delay the passage of the bill. Hold on = wait/grip; hold out = resist/offer; hold down = suppress or keep at a low level.

questions.stem: 'The investigation ______ several previously unknown facts about the case.' The correct phrasal verb is:
questions.explanation: BRING UP = to raise or mention something. 'The investigation brought up several unknown facts' = revealed/raised them. Came up with = invented; threw out = discarded; put down = wrote/criticised.

questions.stem: 'The government decided to ______ the new taxation scheme after public backlash.' The correct phrasal verb is:
questions.explanation: A is correct. BACK OUT OF = to withdraw from a commitment or plan. 'Decided to back out of the scheme after backlash' = chose to withdraw from/cancel the scheme due to public opposition. Back up = support; back down = concede; set back = delay.
